fields.v: Pan, R., Zhang, J., Wu, L., Zhang, Y., Zhang, H., Zhang, L. (2026). Do Modifications Made by Coding Agents Make Subsequent Software Maintenance Harder? arXiv:2610.14768v1 [cs.SE], 10 Oct 2026
Preprint — arXiv:2610.14768v1 [cs.SE], 10 Oct 2026; no published venue stated
Peking University, China (Pan, Wu, L. Zhang); University of New South Wales, Australia (J. Zhang); Harbin Institute of Technology (Shenzhen), China (Y. Zhang); Chongqing University, China (H. Zhang)

Proposes an evaluation method; secondary: Evaluates — paired evaluation design (each later maintenance task run from the developers' history and from the agent's own history) and benchmark SWE-Maintain (100 three-event episodes, 50 Python repositories), used in an empirical study of five coding systems with two backbone models (1,996 paired later events)

rev.why: The contributions list the paired design and the SWE-Maintain benchmark first, but the title and the central question are empirical (does agent-written code make later maintenance harder?) and most of the paper is the RQ1-RQ3 study. 'Evaluates; secondary: Proposes an evaluation method' is an equally defensible reading.

fields.warn: O título e a questão central são empíricos (RQ1–RQ3), mas as contribuições põem primeiro o desenho emparelhado e o benchmark. Decide se a natureza principal é Proposes an evaluation method ou Evaluates.

fields.v: No SDD approach evaluated. Coding systems: Mini-SWE-Agent, Agentless, SE-Agent, OpenHands, Claude Code (versions not given in the paper; 'framework versions ... are reported in our repository'); backbone models GPT-5.6-Luna and DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731. Settings compared: Developer-History vs Agent-History

Task input per event: a maintenance instruction reconstructed from the commit message and linked PR/issue (median 24 words); hidden tests never shown to the agent; developer reference patch used only for validation and the Developer-History state

Not prescribed. Each event runs in a fresh session; agents use their own loops (Agentless: fixed pipeline of fault localization, patch generation, patch validation). Episode: E1 → E2 → E3, the repository carried forward under Agent-History
None during agent runs (autonomous). In benchmark construction, two human reviewers who are not authors inspect every instruction against four criteria
N/A (no SDD approach); coding agents run on natural-language maintenance instructions
Not classifiable (no SDD approach; authors' wording: 'maintenance instruction', 'hidden tests specify the required behavior of each event')

Existing code bases: sequential maintenance events (bug fixes 90, feature additions 81, behaviour changes 69, configuration/schema 17, API compatibility 14, error handling 12, dependency/build 10, other 7)

50 repositories, 100 episodes, 300 events (200 later events); 1,996 paired later events evaluated. Python LOC per repository median 1,744 [IQR 977-5,208], range 160-128,632; modules median 14; reference patch median 1 non-test file and 17 non-test lines
Open-source Python repositories: developer tools 16, CLI tools 8, HTTP clients 7, libraries 7, data processing 5, infrastructure 4, frameworks 3
N/A (autonomous agents, no participants). Two non-author human reviewers of instructions; profile Not stated

Maintenance effort: consumed tokens and model requests, compared only on events resolved (ER) under both settings as the per-event log ratio log((e_A+1)/(e_D+1)); median with clustered bootstrap interval

Task Resolution Rate (TR: passes the current event's hidden tests; reported for E1, E2, E3, Later TR); Event Resolve Rate (ER: current hidden tests and all earlier events' tests pass; Later ER); Episode Resolve Rate (EpR: all three events resolved under ER, Agent-History only); Average Maintained Events (AME, 0-3)

None as outcome. RQ3 uses six properties of the earlier agent change relative to the developer change as predictors: excess changed LOC, developer file divergence, future-function alignment, change-local cognitive complexity, affected dependents, co-change alignment
None

Classification of inherited test failures (28% no valid change at the previous event, 38% assertion-only, 26% missing names/attributes/signatures, 9% unclassified); pre-solved later tasks (10 events, 1.5%); facilitation and hindrance outcomes (RQ3)

Automatic: hidden F2P/P2P tests run in reproducible environments, same tests and timeout in both settings; token and request counts from runs; repository-clustered bootstrap (10,000 replicates), exact McNemar test, Bayesian mixed-effects models (4 chains × 4,000 iterations). Benchmark construction: two LLM reviewers and two non-author human reviewers check instructions; tests for 108 events written by the authors from the instruction; intent/relation labels by two LLM annotators with adjudication

Success criterion: none stated by the authors for a configuration; quality and cost verdicts for every entry: no criterion stated by the authors. Values on SWE-Maintain (Later TR Dev → Agent; Later ER Dev → Agent; EpR; AME, Agent-History): Mini-SWE-Agent + GPT-5.6-Luna TR 54.5 → 48.0, ER 42.0 → 21.5, EpR 18.0, AME 0.91; Agentless + GPT-5.6-Luna TR 31.0 → 26.0, ER 20.5 → 9.5, EpR 7.0, AME 0.48; SE-Agent + GPT-5.6-Luna TR 55.0 → 46.5, ER 41.5 → 20.5, EpR 17.0, AME 0.88; OpenHands + GPT-5.6-Luna TR 56.0 → 51.0, ER 44.5 → 29.0, EpR 24.0, AME 1.05; Claude Code + GPT-5.6-Luna TR 55.0 → 49.5, ER 41.0 → 24.0, EpR 20.0, AME 1.00; Mini-SWE-Agent + DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 TR 51.5 → 45.5, ER 37.5 → 24.0, EpR 17.0, AME 0.95; Agentless + DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 (98 paired episodes) TR 11.0 → 7.5, ER 4.1 → 1.0, EpR 0.0, AME 0.15; SE-Agent + DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 TR 43.0 → 42.5, ER 29.5 → 18.0, EpR 13.0, AME 0.73; OpenHands + DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 TR 48.0 → 42.0, ER 37.0 → 24.5, EpR 17.0, AME 0.92; Claude Code + DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 TR 51.0 → 41.5, ER 38.0 → 23.5, EpR 19.0, AME 0.89. Effort: median log token ratio +0.03 overall; OpenHands +0.18 (about 19% more tokens on its own history)

Tasks: 200 later events of SWE-Maintain (1,996 paired events). Compared: Developer-History (start from developers' preceding patches, as in SWE-bench) vs Agent-History (start from the agent's own preceding changes), for 10 system × model combinations. Baseline: Developer-History. Held constant within a combination: instruction, backbone model and configuration, execution environment, stopping rule, execution limits, hidden tests; fresh session per event. Acceptance tests: hidden certified F2P/P2P tests (cumulative gold replay). Repetitions: one run per setting per event; E1 (identical start in both settings) used as reference for run-to-run variation. Human intervention: none

Agent-History lowers Later TR in all 10 combinations by 0.5-9.5 points: overall −5.6 [95% CI −7.2, −4.1] vs +1.8 [0.0, +3.7] at E1. Later ER lower in all 10 by 3.1-21.0: 33.6% → 19.6% (−14.0 [−16.1, −11.9]); 346 events resolved only under Developer-History vs 66 only under Agent-History. TR gap grows from 4.0 (E2) to 7.2 (E3). Effort on 325 events resolved in both: median log token ratio +0.03 [−0.03, +0.08]. RQ2: 1,349 events (68%) start from code failing earlier tests: ER 23.7 → 1.9 (−21.9), TR −7.6; on 647 events passing earlier tests ΔER +2.3 [−0.9, +5.5]; excluding pre-solved (619) +2.7 [−0.5, +6.1], McNemar p = 0.09. RQ3: future-function alignment associated with facilitation (0.77 [0.14, 1.83]) and 14% fewer tokens; no property associated with hindrance

Yes per the authors: the paired design separated the effect of the starting history from task difficulty, with the direction consistent across all 10 combinations and run-to-run variation bounded by the E1 difference (+1.8). Repeatability: one run per setting; aggregate inference only. Limitations stated: single run per event; Developer-History code may be in pretraining data; RQ2 cohorts differ in difficulty; tests are incomplete specifications; 137 instructions restated from short commit titles; RQ3 exploratory and observational (53 and 36 events)

Limitations: one run per setting; possible pretraining exposure favouring Developer-History; hidden tests not complete specifications and some encode developer interfaces; 137 of 300 instructions from short commit titles; episodes skip intermediate commits; 108 events use author-written tests; only Python, 3-event chains, five systems, two models; no study of agents building on another agent's or mixed human-agent histories; RQ3 associations exploratory. Gaps / future work: measure failure propagation (how long unrepaired failures survive) with longer chains; evaluations should run agents from their own history and report accumulated outcomes; agents should run earlier tests before declaring done

Benchmark, harness and all agent trajectories said to be released and exact model parameters, framework versions and limits 'reported in our repository', but no repository URL appears in the text. No pre-registration. Inconsistency: text and Table 1 say 9 application domains, but Table 1 lists 7 domain categories that already sum to 50 repositories (p. 7). Agentless with DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 has 98 of 100 episodes, giving 1,996 rather than 2,000 paired events (p. 10).
